# papyrium.model.star_lc10

The Star LC-10 Multi-Font and LC-10 Colour, 9-pin dot-matrix printers
of the late 1980s, for
Papyrium, in its Standard mode, in which it follows the Epson LX-800,
speaking ESC/P through `papyrium.language.escp`. `docs/star-lc-10.md`
records the behaviour from Star's manuals, and `docs/star-lc10-firmware.md`
what the LC-10 Colour's firmware shows.

It prints with the LC-10's own characters, from `papyrium.font.lc10`, and
forms them as its firmware does: draft, with pica made from the Sanserif
typeface at half width and elite from the ROM's draft table; and four
near letter quality typefaces, Courier, Sanserif, and Orator with small
capitals or with lower case, each in pica and elite, printed in two
passes half a dot apart, at fixed pitch or proportionally spaced. Italic
slants every character, draft and NLQ, as the firmware does, each
column's dots moving further right the higher they are. The IBM block graphics are twelve dots high, as the
printer prints them, so that boxes join at 1/6 inch line spacing.

## Demonstration page

<img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/master/docs/images/demo-star-lc10.png" alt="The star-lc10 demonstration page" width="100%">

Print it yourself, as PNG and PDF, with `papyrium demo star-lc10`; `-M`
options set the printer up, such as `-M stationery=green-bar`.

## The LC-10 Colour

`star-lc10-colour` is the LC-10 Colour: the LC-10 with a ribbon of four
bands, black, cyan, magenta and yellow. `ESC r` prints in seven colours,
violet, orange and green being the same dots struck through two bands,
which Papyrium's outputs mix as the inks mix on paper. Commands typed
into the text itself, a letter in doubled parentheses and a digit, set
the type style (`((F))`), size (`((S))`), colour (`((C))`), bold
(`((B))`) and italic (`((I))`); the plain LC-10 obeys only the sheet
feeder's. Its options are the LC-10's.

<img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/master/docs/images/demo-star-lc10-colour.png" alt="The star-lc10-colour demonstration page" width="100%">

## Options

Registered as `star-lc10` on the `papyrium.model` axis. The options model
the printer's DIP switches and paper:

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `form-length` | `11` | Form length in inches (switch 1-1 gives 11 or 12) |
| `auto-carriage-return` | `yes` | A line feed also returns the head to the left margin (switch 1-2) |
| `ibm-mode` | `no` | IBM mode: the IBM Proprinter II's language rather than ESC/P (switch 1-6 off) |
| `graphics-table` | `no` | Standard mode: codes 128-254 from IBM character set #2 rather than italics. IBM mode: character set #1, which obeys codes 128-159 as controls, rather than #2 (switch 1-7 off) |
| `auto-line-feed` | `no` | Each carriage return also feeds a line (switch 1-8 off) |
| `download-characters` | `no` | The RAM holds download characters rather than a 4K input buffer (switch 2-1 off) |
| `character-set` | `usa` | Power-on international set: any of the thirteen `ESC R` sets, by name or number (switches 2-2 to 2-4 give 0-7) |
| `paper-width` | `9.5`, or `8.5` for `sheet` | Paper width in inches, tear-off strips included; the line is centred on it |
| `top-offset` | `19/36` | Inches from the perforation to the top of the first line |
| `stationery` | `fanfold` | The paper: `fanfold` (plain, with tear-off strips), `sheet` (no strips), `green-bar`, `blue-bar`, `music-ruled` |
| `font` | `lc10-draft` | The pica draft characters: an installed font's name, or the path of a dot font file |
| `elite-font` | `lc10-draft-elite` | The elite draft characters: an installed font's name, or the path of a dot font file |

Star's additions to ESC/P are obeyed: absolute and relative positioning
(`ESC $`, `ESC \`), both margins at once (`ESC X`), extra space between
characters (`ESC SP`), moving to a column (`ESC f 0`), the slashed zero
(`ESC ~`), overline (`ESC _`), the top margin (`ESC c`), reverse line
feed and top of page (`ESC LF`, `ESC FF`) and the macro (`ESC +`).
Character sizes print as the LC-10 prints them, always in near letter
quality: double and quadruple size and their halves (`ESC h`), double
height on the base line (`ESC w`), and `ESC [ @`.

Download characters are defined as the LC-10 defines them, in draft or,
with NLQ selected, in NLQ's two-pass grid (`ESC &`, `ESC %`, `ESC :`).

In IBM mode (`-M ibm-mode=yes`) the LC-10 speaks the IBM Proprinter
II's language, built on `papyrium.language.proprinter`: its character
sets 1 and 2 and the commands whose letters it gives other meanings
(`ESC 2`, `4`, `5`, `6`, `7`, `:`, `=`, `A`, `J`, `P`, `Q`, `R`, `\`,
`^`), with Star's `FS` commands for the Standard mode ones they displace.
It keeps its own typefaces, which `ESC I` chooses among (0 draft, 1 draft
elite, 2 Sanserif, 3 or 7 Courier, 4 to 6 from the download set), and the
commands both modes share. As in the firmware, one interpreter speaks
both, so `ESC 0x01` and `ESC 0x02`, which the manual does not mention,
change between Standard and IBM mode part way through a job.
